standard_prerequisites.name: Characterizations of the degree zero cohomology
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the characterizations of the degree zero cohomology through injectivity of the pullbacks to points and through generation of the top cohomology by classes of points
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies what it means for the conditions to fail and shows that the constructed direct summand prevents the comparison map from being an isomorphism.

core_obligations: Reduce to an even negative degree (proof lines 3932-3940): by additivity one may assume the example is irreducible and hence equidimensional; if the degree is odd, replacing the scheme by its product with itself produces an example in an even degree, which can be written as minus twice a positive integer.

Construct the counterexample (proof lines 3940-3951): taking the product of that scheme with the appropriate power of the projective line, the product formula for the cohomology exhibits the degree zero cohomology as containing the direct sum of the degree zero cohomology of the original scheme and the tensor product of its negative degree part with powers of the second cohomology of the projective line, both nonzero; the second summand cannot belong to the image of the degree zero cohomology of the spectrum of the ring of global sections, so the comparison map fails to be an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an irreducible example in an even negative degree.
Multiply by a power of the projective line to move the negative class into the middle degree.
Show the resulting degree zero cohomology is too large for the comparison map to be an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if some cohomology group of a smooth projective scheme is nonzero in a negative degree, then some equidimensional smooth projective scheme fails the equivalent characterizations of the degree zero cohomology (statement lines 3928-3934). The proof (proof lines 3935-3951) reduces to an even negative degree and multiplies by a power of the projective line to exhibit a direct summand of the degree zero cohomology outside the image of the comparison map. H3: a reduction with an explicit construction, written out in full.
